title: OpenAI maps its EU AI Act approach to safety, transparency and provenance
friendlyTitle: OpenAI explains how it plans to follow Europe’s AI rules
summary: OpenAI outlined how its system cards, preparedness processes, external testing and content-provenance work align with the EU’s general-purpose AI and transparency codes. It says it is expanding provenance measures beyond images to audio and, as standards mature, other modalities including text.
friendlySummary: OpenAI described its safety tests, model reports and tools for showing when content was made by AI.
whyItMatters: European customers and developers need practical evidence—not only policy statements—to meet AI governance obligations. Model documentation, risk reporting and provenance signals can become important inputs to vendor selection and compliance work.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Businesses in Europe need clear information about AI systems so they can use them safely and follow the law.
